text: maya: FYI I hit another broken fragment after the MDX migration. Links to headings that come immediately after an image are resolving to a deduped slug (e.g. #release-notes-2) and existing links to #release-notes 404 the anchor. jonathan: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal snippet and the failing link? maya: Snippet from guides/releases.md: ```markdown ![timeline](./assets/release-timeline.png) ### Release notes - bump runtime - update changelog ``` External links that point to /guides/releases#release-notes now fail in linkcheck. rachel: Local `mkdocs build` shows the heading id is `release-notes-1` (slug dedupe). This seems to happen when a non-heading element with no id precedes the heading. sam: CI output: ``` [linkcheck] WARNING: Fragment not found: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/releases#release-notes [docusaurus] ERROR: anchor not found for #release-notes ``` aditya: Short-term options: 1) add explicit HTML anchors above problematic headings; 2) modify our linkcheck to accept deduped slugs temporarily; 3) change existing incoming links. I vote for (1) for minimal risk. maya: Example quick-fix I pushed to a small branch: ```html ### Release notes ``` This restores the old fragment behavior without changing the slugify toy. jonathan: Can you also add a note to docs/migration/MDX-SLUGS.md so folks know headings after media may get dedupe suffixes? That way future PRs can either add anchors or accept the new slugs. rachel: I'll scan the repo for similar patterns with a grep: `git grep -n "!\[" docs/ | cut -d: -f1 | sort -u` then check headings immediately following. We can run `npm run linkcheck` against the preview after the quick fix. sam: docs-bot created a deploy preview for the branch: https://deploy-preview-1177--staging.docs.redwood.ai/guides/releases (build 1177) :white_check_mark: Linkcheck shows the previously failing fragment now resolves. aditya: Good. We should file a follow-up ticket to fix the slugify plugin (consistent dedupe behavior) and add a regression test in our docs CI to catch this pattern. maya: Thanks everyone. Once the PR merges, let's run a full site linkcheck and open follow-up issues for the tooling fix and a migration note.
